feed.title: Combined summary - Subject: Eltoo / LN-Symmetry on Inquisition Signet: BIP 118 + 3-Round State Chain (APO+CTV)

entry.title: Combined summary - Subject: Eltoo / LN-Symmetry on Inquisition Signet: BIP 118 + 3-Round State Chain (APO+CTV)
entry.summary: Recent advancements in Bitcoin's transaction scripting and state management have demonstrated significant progress, especially through the practical application of Eltoo-style state chains utilizing new opcode proposals on Inquisition 29.2 signet. This implementation leverages BIP 118 (APO) for efficient state updates and CheckTemplateVerify (CTV) for secure settlement processes. The underlying structure employs a three-leaf Taproot tree for each state UTXO, with each leaf serving a dedicated verification function: template hash checks, BIP 118 signature validation, and sequence control. Such an architecture upholds the correctness and continuity of state transitions while ensuring that only the latest authorized state can be settled, as previous states are rendered invalid by CTV constraints. The robustness of this system is further underscored by its ability to rebind outputs without resigning, providing strong guarantees over state integrity and minimizing operational overhead. Transaction identifiers were shared at every stage, offering transparency and verifiability for the protocol’s execution. Extensive documentation and source code, including a comprehensive overview of BIP 118 signing primitives and rebinding proof, are available at [delvingbitcoin](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bip-118-signing-from-scratch-on-chain-rebinding-proof/2411), with additional resources on the Eltoo state chain’s construction [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-three-rounds-six-transactions-apo-ctv/2413) and source code examples at [btcaaron](https://github.com/aaron-recompile/btcaaron). Parallel to these developments, Sergio Demian Lerner has revitalized the ln-symmetry branch of CLN, integrating innovations enabled by large language models to accelerate the project’s progression. Detailed recaps and technical insights can be found on the [project recap page](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/ln-symmetry-project-recap/359/17). Lerner’s recent work explores a novel protocol variant combining APO, CSFS, TH, and IK, forming an alternative to the CTV-based approach. While this new variant offers similar functionalities, its deployment on signet remains contingent upon the activation of OP_TEMPLATEHASH, highlighting both the promise and current limitations in experimental environments. Lerner’s technical inquiries into opcode optimization underscore ongoing efforts to refine Bitcoin’s scripting capabilities. His analysis questions whether Taproot Hints (TH) offer tangible benefits beyond those achievable with CTV and CSFS, particularly regarding hash management within scripts. He also seeks clarity on the structural role of Input Keying (IK), probing whether its utility extends beyond byte-saving optimizations to more fundamental scripting enhancements. The exploration includes evaluating if CSFS alone suffices for state binding or if supplementary mechanisms like TH are indispensable. These discussions aim to determine the minimal and most effective opcode set required for robust ln-symmetry channel functionality, with the broader objective of streamlining script complexity, increasing efficiency, and enhancing protocol flexibility. Alternative approaches to Eltoo-like functionality within the Lightning Network are also under consideration. One such method involves OTS-based Payment Channels (OTS-PCs), which avoid the need for consensus changes via soft-forks. Details about this technique are provided in a scholarly article accessible on [Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.04021), offering a research-backed framework for developers interested in novel payment channel constructions and incremental improvements to Lightning Network infrastructure. Substantial progress has been achieved in state chain implementations through the combination of CSFS and CTV, reducing the entire process to just two transactions while retaining Eltoo’s desirable properties. Jeremy Rubin’s CSFS rekey ladder construction enables seamless signature delegation between states, obviating the need for full, separate transactions at each update. This streamlined design collapses the entire chain into a single settlement witness, simplifying both implementation and verification. The operational success of this approach, confirmed on signet with validated transaction IDs, is detailed in Rubin’s explanatory post [here](https://rubin.io/bitcoin/2024/12/02/csfs-ctv-rekey-symmetry/) and further elaborated in a full construction write-up with comprehensive threat analysis and witness layout [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-again-three-rounds-two-transactions-csfs-ctv-with-rekey-and-ladder-no-cat/2430). Source code supporting these advancements is openly accessible at Aaron’s [GitHub repository](https://github.com/aaron-recompile/btcaaron/tree/main/examples/eltoo), inviting deeper technical engagement from the community. Practical experimentation has also extended to the recently enabled OP_TEMPLATEHASH on Inquisition 29.4 signet, where Greg’s draft scripts were used to compare APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV, and CSFS+TH+IK variants within the same multi-party channel setting.
